questions.prompt: Which way do roots grow, and why?
options: Downward into the soil, to anchor the plant and reach water and minerals
Upward toward the sun, to catch light
Outward into the air, to spread seeds
They do not grow at all
questions.explanation: Roots grow downward into the soil. This anchors the plant in place and lets it reach water and minerals underground.
questions.misconception: A common mix-up is thinking roots grow toward light like stems do - but roots grow down into the dark soil because they anchor and absorb, not because they photosynthesize.

questions.prompt: Why do roots have root hairs?
options: They increase the surface area so the root can absorb more water
They make the root stronger against wind
questions.explanation: Root hairs are tiny extensions that greatly increase the root's surface area. More surface area means the root can take in much more water from the soil.
questions.misconception: Some learners think root hairs make the root tough or spiky to hold on. - But their real job is to boost surface area for soaking up water and minerals.

questions.prompt: What covers the very tip of a root, and what does it do?
options: The root cap - it protects the tip as it pushes through the soil
The bark - it keeps water out
questions.explanation: The root cap is a protective covering at the very tip. It shields the delicate growing tip as the root pushes through soil and stones.
questions.misconception: A common error is thinking roots push through soil easily because they are sharp. - Instead the root cap cushions and protects the growing tip from being damaged.

questions.prompt: Does a root photosynthesize (make food from sunlight)?
options: No - roots live in dark soil and have no chloroplasts
Yes - roots are green and make sugar
questions.explanation: Roots grow underground in the dark, so they contain little to no chloroplasts and do not photosynthesize. Leaves do the food-making.
questions.misconception: People often assume every greenish plant part makes food. - but photosynthesis needs light, and roots live in darkness underground, so leaves do that job.
